hubs.name: Comodoro Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport

spots.name: La Moneda Palace
spots.summary: La Moneda Palace, or simply La Moneda, is the seat of the president of Chile. It also houses the offices of three cabinet ministries: Interior, General Secretariat of the Presidency, and General Secretariat of the Government.

spots.name: Santiago Metropolitan Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santiago Metropolitan Cathedral is the seat of the Archdiocese of Santiago and the main temple of the Catholic Church in that country. As a Cathedral Church, it is the permanent seat of the Archbishop of Santiago and is dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary.

names.fr: Cathédrale métropolitaine de Santiago du Chili

spots.name: Santa Lucía Hill
spots.summary: Santa Lucía Hill, also known in Mapuche as Huelén Hill, is a hill in the centre of Santiago, Chile. It is situated between Alameda del Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins in the south, Santa Lucía Street in the west and Victoria Subercaseaux on the east. An adjacent metro station is named after it.

spots.name: San Cristóbal Hill
spots.summary: San Cristóbal Hill is a hill in northern Santiago, Chile. It rises 880 m AMSL and about 300 m above the rest of Santiago; the peak is the third highest point in the city, after Cerro Manquehue and Cerro Renca.

spots.name: Gran Torre Costanera

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gran Torre Costanera, previously known as Costanera Center Torre 2, also known as El Costanera by locals, and previously known as Torre Gran Costanera, is a 62-story skyscraper in Santiago, Chile.

names.ja: グラントーレ・サンティアゴ

spots.name: Chilean National Museum of Fine Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chilean National Museum of Fine Arts, located in Santiago, Chile, is one of the major centers for Chilean art and for broader South American art. Established in 1880, the organization is managed by the Artistic Union.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Chilean National Museum of Fine Arts

spots.name: O'Higgins Park

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: O'Higgins Park, formerly known as Cousiño Park and originally as Campo de Marte, is an urban park of roughly 75 to 80 hectares in the Santiago Commune, in the center of Santiago, Chile. It is Santiago's second-largest public park after Metropolitan Park, and one of the city's principal "green lungs."

spots.name: Iglesia de San Francisco, Santiago de Chile
spots.summary: The San Francisco Church is a Franciscan church on Avenida Libertador General Bernardo O'Higgins, in the downtown of Santiago de Chile. The church, along with the adjacent convent, is one of the oldest colonial-era buildings in the country. It has been resistant to about 15 earthquakes of magnitude over 7.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Iglesia de San Francisco, Santiago de Chile

spots.name: Plaza de Armas
spots.summary: The Plaza de Armas is the main square of Santiago, the capital of Chile. Plaza de Armas metro station is located under the square.

spots.name: Costanera Center
spots.summary: The Costanera Center is a commercial and business complex located in the commune of Providencia, Santiago, Chile. Owned by Cencosud, the complex consists of four skyscrapers, including the Gran Torre Santiago, two high-end hotels, an office building, and a six-floor shopping mall.

spots.name: Plaza Baquedano
spots.summary: Plaza Baquedano, commonly known as Plaza Italia, is a major landmark in Santiago, Chile.

spots.name: National Library of Chile

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The National Library of Chile is the national library of Chile. It is located on the Avenida Libertador General Bernardo O'Higgins in Santiago, in a building completed in 1925, though its history reaches to the early nineteenth century before it was relocated to its current home.

spots.name: Santiago General Cemetery
spots.summary: The Santiago General Cemetery in Santiago, Chile, is one of the largest cemeteries in Latin America with an estimated two million burials. The cemetery was established in 1821 after Chile's independence when Bernardo O'Higgins inaugurated the Alameda de las Delicias along the old course of the Mapocho River.

names.ja: サンティアゴ総合墓地

spots.name: Basílica de los Sacramentinos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basílica de los Sacramentinos is a church in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Santiago de Chile. It administered by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament and its design was inspired by the Basilique du Sacré-Cœur in Paris. The main cupola of the church has a structural height of 69 m (226 ft).

spots.name: Chilean National Museum of Natural History

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chilean National Museum of Natural History is one of three national museums in Chile, along with the Museum of Fine Arts and the National History Museum. It is located in Quinta Normal Park, and was founded in 1830 by the French naturalist Claudio Gay.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Chilean National Museum of Natural History

names.nl: Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de Chile
names.fr: Musée national d'histoire naturelle de Santiago
names.ja: チリ国立自然史博物館
names.zh: 智利国家自然历史博物馆

spots.name: Sanctuary on San Cristóbal Hill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sanctuary of the Immaculate Conception on San Cristóbal Hill is one of the principal places of worship for the Catholic Church of Chile, as well as being an icon of Santiago, Chile.

names.zh: 圣克里斯托瓦尔山圣母无玷始胎朝圣地

spots.name: Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art is an art museum dedicated to the study and display of pre-Columbian artworks and artifacts from Central and South America.

names.zh: 智利前哥伦布艺术博物馆

spots.name: Chilean National History Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio de la Real Audiencia de Santiago is a building located on the Plaza de Armas in Santiago, Chile. The building dates back to 1808 and houses, since 1982, the National History Museum of Chile.

spots.name: Basilica de la Merced

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica de la Merced is a basilica located in Santiago, Chile.

spots.name: Barrio París-Londres
spots.summary: Barrio París-Londres is a barrio located in Santiago, Chile. The neighborhood intersects at Calle Londres and Calle París, located behind the San Francisco Church, in its former orchard.

spots.name: Quinta Normal Park

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Quinta Normal Park is an urban park in the city of Santiago, Chile. The park is located in the Commune of Santiago with its namesake commune, Quinta Normal, situated just outside the park across the communal boundary.

names.ja: キンタ・ノルマル公園

spots.name: Former National Congress Building
spots.summary: The Former National Congress Building is the former home of the Chilean Congress. Congress met in this building in central Santiago until Salvador Allende's socialist government was overthrown by Augusto Pinochet's military coup d'état on September 11, 1973.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Former National Congress of Chile building

names.es: Edificio del ex Congreso Nacional de Chile
names.it: Palazzo dell'ex Congresso Nazionale del Cile

spots.name: Londres 38

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Londres 38 is a building that was used by the National Intelligence Directorate (DINA) as a detention and torture center for opponents of Augusto Pinochet's dictatorship. The facility is located in downtown Santiago, Chile, and was known in DINA's jargon by the code name Yucatán.

spots.name: Titanium La Portada

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Titanium La Portada is an office building in Santiago, Chile. Located in the capital's high-end financial district of El Golf, it is the second tallest skyscraper in the country. Construction began in January 2007, and was completed in January 2010.

spots.name: Iglesia San Agustín, Chile

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Iglesia de San Agustín — Our Lady of Grace, commonly known as Church of St Augustine or Templo de San Agustín, is owned by the Order of Saint Augustine. It is a Catholic church, located at the southeast corner of Agustinas and Estado streets, in downtown Santiago, Chile.

spots.name: Bernardo O'Higgins Military School
spots.summary: The Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins Military Academy, commonly known as the Military Academy, is the institution responsible for training officers for the Chilean Army. Its graduates enter the officer corps with the rank of ensign (alférez).

names.fr: École militaire du Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins
names.es: Escuela Militar del Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins
names.ja: リベルタドール・ベルナルド・オイギンス陸軍士官候補生学校

spots.name: Plaza de la Ciudadanía
spots.summary: La Moneda Palace, or simply La Moneda, is the seat of the president of Chile. It also houses the offices of three cabinet ministries: Interior, General Secretariat of the Presidency, and General Secretariat of the Government.

spots.name: Basílica del Salvador

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basílica del Salvador is a basilica located at the corner of Huérfanos Street and Almirante Barroso Street in the Barrio Brasil of Santiago de Chile. The basilica was designed by the German architect Teodoro Burchard in the Neo Gothic style. It was renovated by Josué Smith Solar in 1932.

names.fr: Basilique du Saint-Sauveur de Santiago du Chili

spots.name: Torre Entel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Torre Entel is the name of a 127.4 metres (418 ft) high TV and telecommunications tower in Santiago, Chile. Torre Entel has an observation deck open for visitors. Construction began in 1970 during Eduardo Frei Montalva term as president and it was inaugurated in 1974.

spots.name: Museum of Memory and Human Rights
spots.summary: The Museum of Memory and Human Rights is a museum in Santiago, Chile, which commemorates the victims of human rights violations during the military dictatorship led by Augusto Pinochet between 1973 and 1990.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Memory and Human Rights

names.de: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
names.fr: Musée de la mémoire et des droits de l'homme
names.es: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
names.it: Museo della memoria e dei diritti umani

spots.name: Plaza de la Constitución
spots.summary: The Plaza de la Constitución is a plaza occupying a full square block in the heart of the civic district of Santiago, Chile.

spots.name: Church of the Vera Cruz

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Iglesia de la Vera Cruz or de la Veracruz is a Catholic church located in Barrio Lastarria in the center of Santiago, Chile.

spots.name: Municipal Theatre of Santiago
spots.summary: The Teatro Municipal, National Opera of Chile is the most important stage theatre and opera house in Santiago, Chile.

names.fr: Teatro Municipal de Santiago de Chile
names.ja: サンティアゴ市立劇場

spots.name: Alameda
spots.summary: Avenida Libertador General Bernardo O'Higgins, popularly known as 'La Alameda', is the main avenue of Santiago, Chile. It runs east–west in the centre of the greater urban area and is 7.77 km (4.83 mi) long, and it has up to 5 lanes in each direction. It was named after Chile's founding father Bernardo O'Higgins.

names.ja: アベニーダ・アラメダ・リベルタドール・ベルナルド・オイヒンス
names.zh: 贝尔纳多·奥希金斯将军解放者大道

spots.name: Central Post Office Building
spots.summary: The Central Post Office Building is a historic post office building on the northern edge of the Plaza de Armas, in Santiago, Chile. It is adjacent to the Palacio de la Real Audiencia de Santiago and is located on what was the land lot originally owned by Pedro de Valdivia and where he built his house.

names.ja: サンティアゴ中央郵便局

spots.name: Casa Colorada
spots.summary: Casa Colorada is a colonial house located in Santiago, Chile. It was built in 1769, by Joseph de la Vega for Mateo de Toro Zambrano, then transferred to the Irarrazaval Family and currently houses the Museo de Santiago. The house has a clay-tiled roof, balconied windows, and deep-red walls, and consists of two storeys.

spots.name: Palacio de la Real Audiencia de Santiago
spots.summary: The Palacio de la Real Audiencia de Santiago is a building located on the Plaza de Armas in Santiago, Chile. The building dates back to 1808 and houses, since 1982, the National History Museum of Chile.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Palacio de la Real Audiencia de Santiago

spots.name: Palacio de los Tribunales de Justicia de Santiago
spots.summary: The Palacio de los Tribunales de Justicia de Santiago is the building housing the Supreme Court of Chile, the Court of Appeals of Santiago, and the Court-martial Court of the Chilean Army, Chilean Air Force and Carabineros de Chile. It occupies a full block-front of Compañía Street between Bandera and Morandé Streets.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Palacio de los Tribunales de Justicia de Santiago

spots.name: Santiago Museum of Contemporary Art

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Santiago Museum of Contemporary Art is located in Santiago, Chile. It is one of the city's major museums, created in 1947, and is run by the University of Chile Faculty of Arts. Since 2005, the museum has had two separate sites: MAC Parque Forestal and MAC Quinta Normal Park.

names.es: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago

spots.name: Centro Cultural La Moneda
spots.summary: Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda is a cultural facility located in Santiago, Chile, under Plaza de la Ciudadanía, in the southern façade of the Palacio de La Moneda.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda

names.nl: Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda

spots.name: National Archives of Chile
spots.summary: The National Archives of Chile is a public organization of the Chilean State, created in 1927 with the goal to "collect and conserve the archives of the Departments of State and all the documents and manuscripts related to the national history, and to oversee their organization and use".

spots.name: Santo Domingo Church, Santiago de Chile

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Santo Domingo Church is a Dominican church in the historical downtown of Santiago de Chile. It is located at the corner of Santo Domingo Street and 21 de Mayo Street.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Santo Domingo Church, Santiago de Chile

names.fr: Église Saint-Dominique de Santiago du Chili

spots.name: Patio 29
spots.summary: Patio 29 is a common grave site in Santiago General Cemetery in Chile, where political prisoners, especially those who "disappeared" during the 1973 Chilean coup d'état, were buried anonymously.

spots.name: Barrio Concha y Toro
spots.summary: Barrio Concha y Toro is a barrio in Santiago, Chile, with a medieval-like street plan influenced by the ideas of Camillo Sitte. The houses are built on the former site of the Díaz Gana Palace's park, which was divided into lots in 1915.

spots.name: Equestrian statue of Pedro de Valdivia

names.es: Estatua ecuestre de Pedro de Valdivia

spots.name: Palacio Cousiño
spots.summary: The Palacio Cousiño is a palace that was designed and built for Isidora Goyenechea, widow of Luis Cousiño, who in turn was son of Matías Cousiño. It is located at 438 Dieciocho Street in Santiago, Chile.

spots.name: Basilica of Lourdes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Lourdes is a church in Santiago, Chile. It stands laterally opposite the Quinta Normal Park.

names.de: Basilika Unserer Lieben Frau von Lourdes
names.es: Basílica de Nuestra Señora de Lourdes
names.zh: 圣地亚哥露德圣母圣殿

spots.name: Mercado Central de Santiago
spots.summary: The Mercado Central de Santiago is the central market of Santiago de Chile. It was opened in 1872 and Fermín Vivaceta was in charge of its construction. The market replaced the Plaza del Abasto, which was destroyed by a fire in 1864.

spots.name: Torre Telefónica Chile
spots.summary: Torre Telefónica Chile formerly known as Edificio CTC is an office skyscraper in the Providencia district of Santiago, Chile. Built between 1993 and 1996, the tower stands at 143 m (469 ft) tall with 34 floors and is the current 3rd tallest building in Chile.

spots.name: Pereira Palace
spots.summary: The Palacio Pereira is a historic neoclassical mansion located at the corner of San Martín and Huérfanos streets, in downtown Santiago, Chile. Built in the second half of the 19th century, it was declared a National Historic Monument in 1981, but this didn't prevent its deterioration.

spots.name: Casa Central de la Universidad de Chile
spots.summary: The Casa Central de la Universidad de Chile, also known as Palacio de la Universidad de Chile, is the main building for the Universidad de Chile, and is located at 1058 Alameda Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins, in Santiago, Chile.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Casa Central de la Universidad de Chile

spots.name: Bernardo O'Higgins Monument
spots.summary: The Bernardo O'Higgins monument is a bronze sculpture on a marble base that represents the moment in which Bernardo O'Higgins crossed over a defeated enemy of the royalist troops with his horse in the Battle of Rancagua in 1814.

spots.name: Iglesia de la Divina Providencia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Iglesia de la Divina Providencia is a church managed by the Sisters of Providence, in Santiago, Chile. It gives its name to the district of Providencia and also to Avenida Providencia.

spots.name: Parque de la Familia
spots.summary: Parque de la Familia is a public park located in the commune of Quinta Normal in Santiago, Chile. It is part of the "Santiago integrated park system" that also included Parque Forestal and Parque de Los Reyes.

spots.name: José Domingo Cañas Memory House
spots.summary: The José Domingo Cañas Memory House is a site of memory in the Ñuñoa district of Santiago, Chile, built on the site of a former clandestine detention and torture center operated by the National Intelligence Directorate (DINA) at 1367 José Domingo Cañas Street.

spots.name: Bustamante Park
spots.summary: Bustamante Park is an urban park in Providencia and Ñuñoa, communes of Santiago, Chile. It occupies the former right-of-way of a railway connecting Santiago with Puente Alto and the site of the former Pirque, or Providencia, railway station.

spots.name: Fuente de Neptuno, Santiago de Chile
Edificio de la Intendencia Metropolitana de Santiago
spots.summary: The Edificio de la Intendencia Metropolitana is a government building housing the Intendencia for the Santiago Metropolitan Region, in Santiago, Chile.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Edificio de la Intendencia Metropolitana de Santiago

spots.name: Paseo Bulnes
spots.summary: Paseo Bulnes is a pedestrian street in downtown Santiago. It runs from Alameda Avenue in the north to the Almagro Park in the south.

spots.name: Parque Quinta Normal

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the city's largest and most traditional parks, with many museums located in and around it. These include the National Museum of Natural History of Chile, the Museum of Science and Technology, the Railway Museum of Chile. Its surroundings are also the Artequín Museum, the Museum of Memory and Human Rights, the Matucana 100 Cultural Center, and Library of Santiago.

spots.name: Estación Central de Santiago
spots.summary: The country's main railway station, designed by Gustave Eiffel is past its glory days as rail transport has been replaced by planes, buses and cars. Still, this remarkable building is where you will arrive at if you travel to Santiago by train and worth seeing even if you don't. Plus, it has even given the name to the neighborhood it's located in!

spots.name: Vega central de Santiago

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A colorful market with over 500 stalls, selling fruits, vegetables and other food products. The current market building was inaugurated a century ago but farmers have been selling their products at this place since colonial times. Worth visiting for the experience.

spots.name: Bar Liguria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This bar looks like a 1950s American diner and plays music ranging from classic 1950s rock to what you'd hear in a mid-2000s London pub. For all that, it's clearly no tourist trap and the clientele are mainly local. At the weekend the bars on Pio Nono are probably a better bet, but for a mid-week drink this is well worth a visit. It is also a great restaurant during the day. It serves many local d

spots.name: Viña Santa Carolina

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in 1875, it's now listed as a national monument. Tours are available for 10 persons or above, call them at least three days in advance. The tour goes through houses and cellars and includes wine tasting. The entrance is approximately 600 m from the Rodrigo Araya metro station.

names.es: Bodegas de la viña Santa Carolina

spots.name: Black Rock Pub

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: An Australian-owned gastropub which offers a wide selection of domestic and international microbrews and cuisine. Watch sports on the multiple TVs inside or enjoy watching the day go by in the tree-shaded terrace. Happy Hour until 22:00 everyday.

spots.name: El Candil

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A quiet bar/restaurant in Providencia. The traffic outside is noticeable but not excessive and drinking outside here has a genuinely pleasant urban flavour. If you fancy making a night of it, Bar Liguria is practically next door.

spots.name: Pio Nono

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pio Nono in Bellavista has an intense feeling, bars line the street on either side. The area has a very youthful quality but older visitors shouldn't be intimidated. One of the most lively areas of the city at the weekend.

spots.name: Boulevard Lavaud

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: In Barrio Yungay, Boulevard Lavaud is more than a coffee and restaurant, is part of Santiago history. Better known as La Peluqueria Francesa, is part restaurant, part antique store and part hair salon

spots.name: Aquí Está Coco

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Seafood is this restaurant's specialty and its menu has a wide variety of fish and shellfish to choose from. There are a number of other dishes for the non-seafood lover as well.

spots.name: Galindo

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: A great place to eat typical Chilean dishes, like "pastel de choclo" or "arrollado huaso", in the middle of Bellavista, typical district of the city nightlife.

spots.name: Ciudad Vieja

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: A great "sanguchería", where you can have some of the most gourmet sandwiches in the city. A place to have a drink with friends at very economical prices.

spots.name: Temple Asian Lounge
spots.summary: One of the best kept secret in Las Condes, this Japanese restaurant offers incredible dishes, like the Karaage or the Onigiri. Great atmosphere, too.

spots.name: Ocean Pacific

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Stylishly blue decorated restaurant that has a broad range of seafood. The take-away parlor next door with the same name, has excellent empanadas.

spots.name: The White Rabbit

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Intimate and charming restaurant, great for romantic dinners. Wonderful food and very friendly staff. Terrific veggie and non-veggie plates.

spots.name: Docetrece
spots.summary: A very good place to eat a generous sandwich (try the "Holanda") or a big Chorrillana, and a great variety of national and imported beers.

spots.name: Fuente Alemana

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: One of the most famous sandwich places in the city, the sandwiches are prepared in the front of the customer. Try the churrasco italiano.

spots.name: Santa Isabel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Big supermarket where you can gather the ingredients for your own meal. It also has simple take-away items such as chicken or rice.

spots.name: Anakena

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Designed to look like an outdoor market with a number of dishes that combine Asian, European, and South American cooking styles.

spots.name: La Casa Club

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Five-level club with each floor catering to different musical tastes, laser show, bar and special events, highly recommended.

spots.name: Nuria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in 1928 with several restaurants around downtown. They have classic Chilean dishes as well as large sandwiches.

spots.name: Batuta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A good spot to see mainstream Chilean rock and metal bands, although it is expensive by Chilean standards.

spots.name: Red Pub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nice bar downtown between lounge bar and more folklorica. Good rock bands often come to play.
